name: Calcium
occurrence: Fifth most abundant element in Earth's crust, mainly as limestone, gypsum, and fluorite.
biologicalRelevance: The main structural mineral in bones and teeth (as calcium phosphate/hydroxyapatite), and its ion signalling triggers muscle contraction and blood clotting.
notableCharacteristics: Reacts with water more gently than sodium or potassium, but still vigorously enough to produce visible hydrogen bubbles.
ncertRelevance: extraction and uses of calcium compounds
whyHere: Losing both 4s electrons gives calcium a stable argon-like Ca²⁺ core, and that ion's small, well-defined charge is exactly why it's so effective as a structural cross-linker in bone mineral and as a signalling trigger in muscle cells.
didYouKnow: Your skeleton is constantly being rebuilt — the calcium in your bones today is fully replaced roughly every ten years through ongoing bone remodeling.
genZNote: Building your skeleton one ion at a time since before you were born. The literal backbone of the operation.
